kings2.19.p1.b1.text: On hearing this report, King Hezekiah tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.

kings2.19.p1.b2.text: And he sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz

kings2.19.p1.b3.text: “This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace; for children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them.

kings2.19.p1.b4.text: … Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives.”

kings2.19.p2.b1.text: “Tell your master that this is what the LORD says: ‘Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.

kings2.19.p2.b2.text: Behold, I will put a spirit in him so that he will hear a rumor and return to his own land, …

kings2.19.p2.b3.text: When the Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found the king fighting against Libnah.

kings2.19.p2.b4.text: Now Sennacherib had been warned about Tirhakah king of Cush: “Look, he has set out to fight against you.” So Sennacherib again sent messengers to Hezekiah,

kings2.19.p3.b1.text: “Give this message to Hezekiah king of Judah: ‘Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying that Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria.

kings2.19.p3.b2.text: Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the other countries, devoting them to destruction. Will you then be spared?

kings2.19.p3.b3.text: Did the gods of the nations destroyed by my fathers rescue those nations—the gods of Gozan, Haran, and Rezeph, and of the people of Eden in Telassar?

kings2.19.p3.b4.text: Where are the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’”

kings2.19.p4.b1.text: So Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers, read it, and went up to the house of the LORD

kings2.19.p4.b2.text: and spread it out before the LORD.

kings2.19.p4.b3.text: “O LORD, God of Israel, enthroned between the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.

kings2.19.p5.b1.text: Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see. …

kings2.19.p5.b2.text: Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria … have cast their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods, but only wood and stone—the work of human hands.

kings2.19.p5.b3.text: And now, O LORD our God, please save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, O LORD, are God.”

kings2.19.p6.b1.text: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah: “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I have heard your prayer concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria.

kings2.19.p6.b2.text: ‘The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.

kings2.19.p6.b3.text: Through your servants you have taunted the Lord, and you have said: “With my many chariots I have ascended to the heights of the mountains, … I have cut down its tallest cedars, …

kings2.19.p7.b1.text: Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should crush fortified cities into piles of rubble.

kings2.19.p7.b2.text: Therefore their inhabitants, devoid of power, … are like plants in the field, … scorched before it is grown.

kings2.19.p7.b3.text: But I know your sitting down, your going out and coming in, and your raging against Me.

kings2.19.p7.b4.text: I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth; I will send you back the way you came.’

kings2.19.p8.b1.text: And this will be a sign to you, O Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows on its own, and in the second year what springs from the same. But in the third year you will sow and reap; you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

kings2.19.p8.b2.text: And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah will again take root below and bear fruit above.

kings2.19.p8.b3.text: ‘He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He will not come before it with a shield or build up a siege ramp against it.

kings2.19.p8.b4.text: He will go back the way he came, … ‘I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.’”

kings2.19.p9.b1.text: And that very night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians.

kings2.19.p9.b2.text: When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!

kings2.19.p10.b1.text: So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.

kings2.19.p10.b2.text: One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to the sword

kings2.19.p10.b3.text: and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esar-haddon reigned in his place.
